stem: Meena waters the tulsi plant on her balcony every morning. Her grandmother says the plant, the soil, the sunlight and the water all work together to keep this small system balanced. Which statement about how this balance is maintained is correct?

options.text: Only living things like the tulsi plant and insects are needed for balance; soil, sunlight and water do not play any part.
Balance is maintained because living things depend on one another and on non-living things: the plant uses sunlight and water, insects take nectar, and decomposers in the soil return nutrients.
Balance is maintained only when plants and insects live in the same place, whether or not nutrients are returned to the soil.
The balance would remain the same if all the water and sunlight were removed, because the tulsi plant is a living thing.

teacher.key_rationale: Ecosystem balance requires both living and non-living components working together: producers make food, consumers feed on them, decomposers return nutrients, and air, water and sunlight support the whole cycle. Only option B states this interdependence. Option A wrongly excludes non-living parts, option C treats mere coexistence as balance, and option D wrongly claims balance survives removal of non-living factors.
